items.headline: IMF board to review Sri Lanka on Dec 2
items.summary: The IMF Executive Board will take up Sri Lanka's seventh Extended Fund Facility review and Article IV consultation on December 2, a decision that governs release of the next tranche. A staff-level deal was reached in early October.

items.headline: Sri Lanka, Thailand sign visa-free travel deal
items.summary: The two countries signed an agreement waiving visas for ordinary passport holders during Thai Deputy PM and Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow's meeting with President Dissanayake. Talks also covered trade, tourism, investment and agriculture.

items.headline: Teachers, principals to report sick on Nov 30
items.summary: A teachers' and principals' union alliance told the Education Ministry its members will take sick leave islandwide on November 30, saying the 2027 Budget failed to settle salary and allowance demands.

items.headline: Port fuel leak fouls Mutuwal coastline
items.summary: Marine gas oil leaking from a port tanker and a terminal pipeline flowed through a drain into the sea, polluting more than 3 km of the Mutuwal/Muthuwela coast. The leak has been stopped and the Coast Guard and Ports Authority are using booms to clean up.

items.headline: Teen drowns off Bentota
items.summary: A 16-year-old died after five youths got into difficulty about 200 m offshore at Bentota; the Coast Guard rescued the other four.

items.headline: PM urges prevention focus for dental service
items.summary: Marking the Government Dental Service's centenary, PM Harini Amarasuriya called for more emphasis on preventive care, early diagnosis and equal access.

items.headline: Deputy minister dismisses critics who lost privileges
items.summary: Fisheries Deputy Minister Rathna Gamage told an Akmeemana gathering not to be swayed by complaints from groups that lost privileges, saying development gains will be shared.

items.headline: New Navy Deputy Chief of Staff
items.summary: Rear Admiral Dammika Wijewardana was named Navy Deputy Chief of Staff from today, while keeping his Northern Naval Area and Chief Hydrographer roles.

items.headline: Minister awaits post-mortem on tusker Kavantissa
items.summary: Environment Minister Dhammika Patabendi denied saying the tusker died of diarrhoea and said a post-mortem must establish the cause, amid reports of bullet fragments in the animal.

items.headline: Toss mix-up at India A v Pakistan A
items.summary: At the Asia Cup Rising Stars in Doha, the match official first named India A as toss winners, then corrected it to Pakistan A after their captain objected; Pakistan A chose to bat.

items.headline: Honda, Toyota recall 1.6m US vehicles
items.summary: The carmakers are recalling about 1.6 million vehicles over Takata airbag inflators that could rupture; no injuries have been reported.

items.headline: Titanic hero's postcard fetches £32,000
items.summary: A postcard sent by a Titanic hero to his sister sold at auction for £32,000, following the sale of a survivor's engagement ring went for £150,000.
